findings.plain: Email that fakes your domain is still delivered: p=none only asks for reports.
findings.fix: Read the reports for a few weeks, fix what fails, then move to p=quarantine and later p=reject.

findings.plain: Monitoring mode without a report address monitors nothing: nobody receives the reports.
findings.fix: Add rua=mailto:<an address you read> to the record.

findings.issue: DKIM was not checked: no selector is listed for this domain.
findings.plain: A DKIM key cannot be found from outside without its selector name.
findings.fix: Open a real email from this domain, find s= in the DKIM-Signature header and add it to dkim_selectors.

label: the author's marketing sending subdomain, delegated to the email tool

findings.issue: No SPF record at this name.
findings.plain: Normal for a subdomain run by an email tool: SPF is checked on the hidden return-path address, not on the visible From address.
findings.fix: Open a real email from this domain and confirm the headers say spf=pass.

findings.issue: No DMARC record at this subdomain: the policy comes from _dmarc.negozio-online.org.
findings.plain: That is how DMARC works for subdomains.
findings.fix: Nothing to do unless this subdomain needs its own policy.

findings.issue: This domain cannot receive email (no MX record).
findings.plain: Replies and bounces sent to an address on this domain are lost.
findings.fix: Use a From and Reply-To address on a domain that receives email, or add MX records.

label: someone else's parked domain: the trap from the field notes

findings.issue: A TXT record answers at _dmarc.mionegozio.com but it is not a DMARC policy ("v=spf1 -all").
findings.plain: A dashboard can show this as verified, yet providers find no policy. The usual cause is a wildcard record on a parked or misconfigured domain.
findings.fix: Check you are working on the right domain, then publish a record that starts with v=DMARC1 at _dmarc.
